# Synthetic decoder regressions

These files were generated for TrueRenderer from numerical constants, without photographs or camera files. They are project test data under the repository license.

`second-ifd-orientation-1.dng` and `second-ifd-orientation-6.dng` extend the synthetic DNG below with an 8×4 JPEG gradient and a separate 1×1 grayscale TIFF image. The primary orientation is explicitly 1; the only byte difference is the second IFD's orientation (1 versus 6). Its value must not rotate the JPEG belonging to the primary IFD. They are generated by the private additional-review fixture script and fingerprinted in `reports/additional-review-windows.json`.

- `plain.tif`: little-endian, uncompressed RGB8 1×1, pixel `[128,128,128]`, no colour tags.
- `linear-srgb.tif`: the same pixel, plus TIFF 6.0 tag 301 (three linear 256-entry tables, each `v*257`), tag 318 (D65 xy 0.3127, 0.3290) and tag 319 (Rec.709 xy primaries). Explicit colour metadata must be applied or refused, never silently converted with sRGB transfer.
- `p3-primaries.tif`: the same pixel, D65 white and P3 xy primaries (0.68,0.32; 0.265,0.69; 0.15,0.06). No transfer table; partial declarations also must not disappear into an assumption.
- `non-bayer-preview.dng`: DNG 1.4, uncompressed LinearRaw RGB16 32×24, constant samples `[1500,1000,800]`, white level 4095, identity colour matrix, unit neutral and D65 illuminant. Tags 513/514 refer to an 8×8 JPEG of a constant RGB colour `(190,130,60)`, generated with System.Drawing. Make/model are synthetic. The development recipe refuses this non-Bayer input; its embedded preview is valid and deliberately has different dimensions.

The fixtures first reproduced defects in the Windows review of 2026-09-14. SHA-256 and observed pre-fix values are preserved in `reports/recheck-windows-2026-09-14.json`; generation script and scratch outputs remain in the private review laboratory.
